necessary_context.content: Definition 1 uses proper closed convex f:R^d→R∪{+∞}, 0≤μ<L≤+∞, finite μ. For corresponding subgradients, ||g1−g2||/L≤||x1−x2||, and f−μ||x||²/2 is convex. Definition 2 requires f(x_i)=f_i and g_i∈∂f(x_i). The extracted scientific records restrict to finite L, where gradients are single-valued, and to finite nonempty data.
necessary_context.name: Function class and interpolation

necessary_context.content: f*(y)=sup_x(<y,x>−f(x)). Theorem 2 exchanges F_{0,L} and F_{1/L,∞} under conjugation. Theorem 3 exchanges F_{μ,L} and F_{0,L−μ} by subtraction of μ||x||²/2. Lemmas 1–2 state the corresponding transformations of interpolation triples.
necessary_context.locator: Section 2.4, PDF p.8; Section 2.5, PDF p.9
necessary_context.name: Conjugation and curvature subtraction
